back: API server (the only front door), etcd (state, replicated with Raft), scheduler (places pods), controller manager (runs the controllers).
kubelet (runs containers via the runtime, runs probes) and kube-proxy (programs Service routing rules).
A controller repeatedly compares desired state with observed state and takes a step to close the gap. Self-healing, eventually consistent.

front: API server down: what still works?
back: Running pods keep serving and Service rules stay. You lose deploys, scaling and rescheduling.
One or more containers scheduled together on one node, sharing an IP and volumes. Disposable: replaced, never repaired.
The scheduler places pods by requests. Limits are enforced by cgroups: memory over limit is OOM-killed, CPU over limit is throttled.

front: maxSurge and maxUnavailable defaults and rounding?
back: 25% each. maxSurge rounds up, maxUnavailable rounds down. 20 replicas: up to 25 pods, at least 15 available.
Stalls; after progressDeadlineSeconds (600 s default) it is marked failed. No automatic rollback: run kubectl rollout undo.
A stable virtual IP and DNS name for pods matching a label selector. Only ready pods are in its endpoints.
kube-proxy picks a pod per connection. One long-lived HTTP/2 connection carries all requests to one pod.
Layer 7 host and path routing rules into the cluster. Does nothing without an ingress controller. Gateway API is the successor.
Pod removed from Service endpoints. Not restarted.
kubelet kills and restarts the container. Check only the process, never a dependency like the database.
Holds off liveness and readiness until the app has started, for slow starters. Restarts the container if it never passes.
periodSeconds 10, timeoutSeconds 1, failureThreshold 3: about 30 s to declare failure.
preStop sleep a few seconds (endpoint removal lags SIGTERM), then drain in-flight requests within terminationGracePeriodSeconds (30 s).
desired = ceil(current × currentMetric / target). 6 pods at 90% with a 60% target = 9. Evaluated every 15 s, 10% tolerance.

front: Why the HPA does not save you from a spike?
back: 15 s cycles plus tens of seconds per pod (minutes if nodes must be added). Use headroom, min replicas and load shedding.
